$comment: GENERATED by mod/tools/catalog.mjs — do not edit by hand. Every id a mod may reference; see mod/README.md.

ability_ended.what: The power winding down: a soft falling sigh into the echo.

ability_started.what: Enabling a powerup: a bright ascending power-up flourish. A rising saw sweep swells underneath a four-note arpeggio (C–E–G–C), capped with a shimmering bell — the unmistakable "power ON" moment.

achievement_legend.what: The fanfare for a LEGEND badge — the sound of the card reveal, in the four beats the light is drawn in: a filtered rip sweeping up over a sub as the rays tear open, a slow choir triad swelling behind them, the badge chime's arpeggio carried two octaves higher and racing the card in, and the full chord landing under the bloom with an impact beneath it. The only achievement cue allowed to stand beside the level-up ding rather than under it.

achievement_unlocked.what: The badge chime, at the middle of the effort ladder — G, C, E climbing 70 ms apart, each triangle note shadowed an octave up by a quiet sine, with a bright airy hiss over the top and a last shimmer rising out of the tail, over a warm root swell and the fifth it settles on. A lesser badge plays the same chime quieter and without those last two; the top rung plays a different piece entirely (achievement_legend).

apparition_vanished.what: An apparition dissolves: a glassy shimmer rising out of hearing, more sigh than event — the figure was never really there.

armor_broke.what: Something rigid giving way — a hard bandpassed crack, a ringing shard above it, then a sawtooth plunging two octaves as the piece falls off.

arrival_parked.what: Somebody parking for a shift, heard from across a car park: the engine sags off and dies, and a beat later a door goes — one flat slam, no cough and no handle rattle. Deliberately thinner and further away than `car_stop`, which is the hero's own car at his elbow; this one is the sound that makes him look up, so it has to read as A CAR, over there, with somebody getting out of it.

asteroid_kill.what: The sky doing your job for you: the impact's boom with a wet crunch folded into it. Distinct from an ordinary takedown on purpose — nobody swung, and the player should be able to hear that the kill was not theirs.

auto_equipped.what: The replacement clacking into the hand (mirrors the UI equip).

badge_swiped.what: A card against the reader at GOODCO's front door: one clean two-tone accept chirp and the servo clunk of the lock letting go. It fires a beat BEFORE the doors themselves move (`door_opened`), because the whole point of the sound is that the player hears the CARD and then watches the building answer it — which is the one thing the level needs him to learn.

bait_detonated.what: The trap paying off: a sharp bandpass crack, a lowpass thump under it, and debris sizzling out behind. Shorter and nastier than a nuke, and pitched up from a slam so the two never blur in a busy fight.

bait_dropped.what: Something tempting hitting the floor: a light metallic clink with a soft ping over it. It has to read as an OBJECT arriving, not as a threat — the threat is bait_detonated, and the gap between them is the whole mechanic.

barrier_absorbed.what: The BLAST SHIELD eating a blow: one glassy tick. This can fire on every contact hit, so it is the quietest sound the game makes.

barrier_broke.what: The shell giving up: a bright shatter — a hard noise crack, then two falling shards. The player must hear that the protection is GONE.

boss_airstrike.what: Something being called down from above: a long falling whistle over a swelling lowpass rumble. The whistle is the tell the player tracks — it falls for most of a second before anything lands, which is exactly the window they have to move.

boss_beam.what: The beam opening and sweeping: a held detuned sawtooth with a bandpass roar riding it, long enough to cover the sweep it describes. One event carries the WHOLE move, so this is one long sound rather than a per-frame texture — the loudest thing the boss does, and it should be.

boss_defeated.what: The giant coming down: a long rumble under descending detuned saws, ending in a floor-shaking thud.

boss_flag_planted.what: A claim staked in the floor: a hard bandpass thunk of the pole going in, then a held square note ringing out over it. Ceremonial — the boss is making a statement, and the ring is the statement.

boss_fled.what: The coward's exit: reality unzipping — a long rising saw sweep with a glassy shimmer on top, snapped shut by a bright crack instead of a corpse hitting the floor.

boss_healed.what: The health bar going the wrong way: a rising sine swell with a sour detuned saw under it. Consonant on top and sour underneath on purpose — it is a heal, and it is bad news, and the sound should carry both.

boss_horde.what: The call that brings everything else in the room: a low detuned saw horn with a long rise and a heavy echo. Architectural rather than personal — the ROOM is answering, and the player should hear the fight get bigger before they see it.

boss_lockdown.what: The shutters coming down: a heavy mechanical slam repeated twice, with a low boom under the second. This is the room becoming a cage, so it is blunt and final rather than musical.

boss_lockdown_lifted.what: The shutters going back up: the lockdown's slam run in reverse — a rising mechanical slide with the pressure releasing behind it. Relief, and short: the fight is still on.

boss_recompile.what: The thing rebuilding itself: a stuttering square ladder climbing in steps, glitchy and quantised, with a thin digital hiss under it. The only sound in the bank that is deliberately MECHANICAL rather than physical — this is software repairing software.

boss_rite_began.what: THE DEATH RITE opening. A long low swell with a detuned saw underneath and a glassy fifth over the top, all on a heavy echo send — the biggest, slowest sound the game makes. The boss is not fighting any more; something else is starting, and the mix should make room for it.

boss_rite_ended.what: The rite closing: the opening swell inverted — everything falls and thins out, and the echo is left to carry the tail. Resolves downward and lands on a clean consonant note, so the room reads as SAFE again.

boss_rite_exit_opened.what: The way out appearing. A rising consonant triangle pair with a glass octave and a wide echo — the first genuinely warm sound after the rite, and the cue the player has been waiting for. Deliberately the reward shape (rising, consonant, sparkling) rather than the door shape.

boss_rite_struck.what: A beat of the rite landing: a bright bandpass crack over a short lowpass boom. This is the one part of the rite the player must react to, so it is the sharpest thing in the sequence — everything else around it is slow.

boss_rite_vanished.what: It is not here any more: a swept highpass whisper going up and out with a sine chasing it. Weightless, and the only thing in the rite with no low end at all — the absence of body is what makes it read as disappearance.

boss_volley.what: A fan of shots leaving at once: three quick square launches stepped 60 ms apart over a lowpass push. Stepped rather than simultaneous because a simultaneous volley is one loud shot — the stagger is what makes the player hear COUNT.

cache_given.what: THE CACHE arriving: a long shimmering swell that rises rather than strikes — a low drone opening under two voices climbing a fifth apart, a wash of high-passed noise gathering over the top, and a bright bell landing on the snap at the end, when the chest is finally a thing in the room. Wet with echo, and pitched clear of the handover's coin figure so the two layer instead of clashing.

car_departed.what: The car pulling away without you: a lowpass engine note falling and thinning out, with the road hiss going with it. Everything in it recedes, which is the whole message.

car_start.what: The hero turns the key on a thirty-year-old hatchback: the starter motor cranks — a dry whirr with three low square coughs riding it — then the engine CATCHES: a saw swell climbing out of the floor into the idle the running `carEngine` rumble takes over from.

car_stop.what: The hero switches the thirty-year-old hatchback off and gets out: the idle sags away down the scale as the engine dies, one last dry cough after it lets go, and the door handle clacks. The mirror of `car_start` — shorter, because a car takes longer to talk into life than out of it.

clean_slate_used.what: A build wiped and handed back: a downward glass sweep, then a single clean sine settling — the descent is the old build coming apart and the note is the empty sheet. Big echo; this happens once in a very long while.

companion_dismissed.what: Sending somebody away: the joining flourish turned around — two triangle notes falling, with the echo left open behind them. Quiet and a little sad, which is the honest reading of the moment.

companion_downed.what: A companion beaten to its knees: a dull body-drop thud under a short falling tone — heavy, but under playerHurt's ceiling (an ally, not the hero).

companion_healed.what: Patching up whoever is following you: a warm rising sine pair with a soft attack. Deliberately rounder and quieter than the hero's own medkit — this is care given, not taken.

companion_joined.what: A spared figure takes the hero's side: a warm little oath — a rising third with a glassy top, brighter than the dialogue knock but far short of a jingle (the joining scene follows anyway).

companion_leveled_up.what: Your companion getting better at this: a small three-note triangle rise. It is the hero's level-up fanfare in miniature and a fifth of the volume — same shape, so it is legible as a ding; much smaller, so it never competes with the player's own.

companion_revived.what: Back on its feet: the downed thud inverted — a quick rising triangle with a soft top, more relief than fanfare.

corpse_recovered.what: Getting your things back off your own body: a soft rising triangle pair with a breath of echo. Consonant and warm — it is a relief, not a triumph, so it sits well under the pickup fanfares.

crate_broken.what: The crate gives way: a wooden crash — a burst of broadband noise (the splintering) over a short falling tone (the box collapsing), a touch meatier than a single hit so the break lands.

crate_hit.what: A blow biting a wooden crate: a short, dry knock — a low filtered thud under a woody click, quiet so a flurry of hits doesn't drown the fight.

defeat.what: The falling minor line with a saw shadow underneath, closed by a dull thud in the dust.

dialogue_started.what: A speaker takes the stage: two knocks with a glassy edge.

door_opened.what: The lock giving way: a heavy clunk, then the slide up and open.

drive_body_a.what: A body meeting the bumper at speed — the FIRST of three, so a road with twenty people on it never plays one sample twenty times. A dull square thud with no ring to it (a person is not a bell), a wet bandpass slap of contact over the top, and a scuff of grit as they go under. Kept quiet: this fires more often than anything else in the minigame.

drive_body_b.what: The second body thud — the same blow caught a touch lower and softer, so a run of hits reads as different people rather than one repeated event.

drive_body_c.what: The third body thud — brighter and shorter, the one that reads as a clipping blow on the wing rather than a square hit on the nose.

drive_body_drag.what: Something has caught under the car and started to travel with it — a long bandpass scrape with a wet lowpass wash beneath it and a slow tail, so the ear places it UNDERNEATH rather than out in front. It runs about as long as a middling drag does; a piece carried further simply has the road noise over the top of it, which is what happens in a real one.

drive_body_hard_a.what: A body taken square at the top end — the sound the arrival lines are refusing to talk about. A sawtooth dive to the floor for the weight of it, a lowpass boom under that, and a short wet burst of contact. Louder than the ordinary thud because the physics says it was: the app picks this over `drive_body_a` off the collision's own joules, not at random.

drive_body_hard_b.what: The second heavy body hit — a shade deeper and longer, with a scatter of highpass debris after it, for the one that came apart over the bonnet.

drive_breakdown.what: The engine giving up in the middle of the road: the note sags away down the scale, the block knocks twice as it dies, and then there is nothing but steam out of a split hose while the wreck rolls to a stop. The mirror of `car_start`'s catch, played backwards and badly.

drive_crunch_a.what: A real collision with another car — the sound that means the drive may be over. Three layers, the way every big impact in the game is built: a saw diving to the floor for the mass of it, a lowpass boom for the air it moved, and delayed highpass sizzle for the glass and trim landing after. Near the mix ceiling, because it is rare and it should frighten.

drive_crunch_b.what: The second heavy collision — the same shape pitched lower and given a metallic wrench in the middle of it, for the hit that folds a wing rather than shattering a light cluster.

drive_crush_a.what: A wheel finding something already lying in the road. The first of three, and the quietest thing on this road that still counts as an event: a short lowpass squelch of the mass giving way, and a dry tick of grit as the tyre climbs back off it. Deliberately small — this fires several times a second in the middle of a blockade, and a crush that announced itself would drown the collision that made the mess.

drive_crush_b.what: The second crush take — the one where something in there was hard. Same squelch, with a short square pop through it for a rib or a skull going under the tread.

drive_crush_c.what: The third crush take — the flattest of them, almost all air: what is left under the wheel this time had already been under one.

drive_debris_clunk.what: The car clouting something dead and steel already lying on the tarmac — a felled street light, kicked on down the road. A hollow triangle bonk with a short metallic ring after it and no crumple at all, which is the whole difference between this and the crunch: nothing here is giving way, it is just being moved.

drive_glass_a.what: A car's windows leaving it — the noise laminated glass makes when a body folds around it, which is not a smash so much as a long bright shatter and then a second of it arriving on the road. Layered OVER the collision that caused it rather than played instead: the crunch is the steel and this is the glass, and they are one event. Bright and thin on purpose, so it sits on top of the smash bank's sub rather than fighting it.

drive_glass_b.what: The second take of a window going — a side pane rather than a screen, so it is a harder, drier burst with far less of it still falling afterwards. Two takes for the same reason the crunch has two: a car with four windows in it can lose them one at a time.

drive_impact_sub.what: THE WEIGHT UNDER A BIG HIT — a bare sub-bass drop with no transient of its own, layered underneath whatever else the collision is playing. It exists because a bank cannot be made bigger by turning it up: the mix has a ceiling and a synthesized crunch hits it long before it sounds heavy. What the ear actually reads as SIZE is energy below about 60 Hz and a tail that outlasts the crack, and neither of those fits inside a sound that also has to be a crack. So the biggest events on this road play their own noise AND this, and the pair is what a lorry-sized collision sounds like. Alone it is almost nothing — which is the test that it is doing its job as a layer rather than as a sound.

drive_panel_a.what: A panel giving up a rung: the dull metallic bonk of a wing folding one step further, with a short click of the seam letting go. Quiet — it plays under a hit that already made its own noise, and is there to tell the player the damage was structural rather than cosmetic.

drive_panel_b.what: The second panel bend — lower and duller, the one that sounds like the car is running out of straight metal to bend.

drive_part_shed.what: A part working free and going: the tear of the last fixing, then the piece skipping away down the tarmac behind — three bright clatters in quick succession, each quieter than the last, so the ear puts it in the mirror rather than on the car.

drive_rollover.what: A car going over — the longest sound on this road, and the only one that is a SEQUENCE rather than an event. A rollover is not an impact: it is a vehicle leaving the ground, coming down on a corner, and then grinding along the tarmac on its roof for the better part of a second. So the layers are laid out in TIME rather than stacked on the same instant — the launch, the first corner landing a beat later, and a long scraping roar under both of them that outlasts them and is what actually says the thing is still going.

drive_scrape_a.what: Trading paint — the wagon's flank against another car's at speed. A bandpass band of grinding noise with a thin metallic squeal sliding down over it, and no low end at all: a scrape is a surface event, and giving it a boom would make every glancing touch read as a crash.

drive_scrape_b.what: The second scrape — shorter and higher, the touch that costs a wing mirror rather than a door.

drive_smash_a.what: THE BIG ONE — two tonnes of estate meeting somebody else's car at the top of the dial, and the loudest thing on this road by a wide margin. The crunch bank above it is a collision; this is a collision that ends somebody's car, and it had to be a shelf of its own because the old top end was a 260 ms saw and a boom, which is a fender-bender at any volume you play it at. Five layers, and the length is doing as much work as the level: a sub-sine falling to nearly nothing for the mass, a detuned saw dive for the structure failing, a long lowpass roar for the air it moved, a hard bandpass crack for the instant of contact, and a slow highpass rain of glass and trim still landing half a second later.

drive_smash_b.what: The second take of the big one — the same collision landing squarer, so it is shorter and harder rather than longer and rounder. Two takes because a driver who is enjoying himself hears this several times a leg, and one take at that rate stops being a collision and starts being a jingle. The sub goes lower and dies sooner, the saw is pitched under the first take's, and the debris tail is drier: less of it in the air, more of it already down.

drive_split_a.what: A bumper going THROUGH somebody rather than merely into them — the sound the heavy body bank cannot make on its own. Three layers in the order the event happens: a bandpass tear that rips upward as the steel parts the body, a hard dry snap of bone under it, and a low wet slump as what is left of them arrives on the tarmac. Louder than the thud it plays over, and it has to be: the two fire on the same tick and this is the one carrying the news.

drive_split_b.what: The second take of a body coming in two — the same three layers pitched and timed differently, so a blockade taken at speed does not play one sample twenty times in four seconds. Wetter and shorter than its sibling: this is the one where the bone gave first.

elevator_locked.what: The call button refusing: a flat mechanical clunk with no travel after it. What sells "locked" is the SILENCE where the motor should have started, so the sound is deliberately over almost before it began.

elevator_ride.what: The car moving: a lowpass motor swell that rises and settles, with a faint cable hiss over it. Long by this bank's standards because the ride is long, and quiet because it is the floor under a transition rather than an event.

elite_cast.what: An elite's move committing: a bright detuned square swell with a glassy octave over it and a long echo send. One sound for every elite primitive — the DRAW says which move it is, and eighteen near-identical casts would be eighteen files nobody could tell apart anyway. Pitched well above the boss material so an elite reads as personal rather than architectural.

enemy_dodge.what: A blow that hit only air: a short dry whiff, no impact body. Quieter and higher than the hero's own dodge so a whiffed swing reads as a near-miss, not a takedown — it fires often, so it stays out of the way.

enemy_enraged.what: Something just got worse: the enrage threshold crossed. A detuned sawtooth climbing and holding, with a slow vibrato on it — the held note is the point, since this is a state change rather than a hit, and the player should feel the fight tilt rather than hear an impact.

enemy_hit.what: Body blow: a mid square thud plus a click of contact.

enemy_hit_crit.what: Body blow: a mid square thud plus a click of contact.

enemy_killed.what: The takedown: a saw dive to the floor, a lowpass boom, and a spray of debris sizzle just behind it.

enemy_killed_crit.what: The takedown: a saw dive to the floor, a lowpass boom, and a spray of debris sizzle just behind it.

enemy_last_words.what: A unique mob's death scene takes the stage: not the arrival knock but a parting breath — a soft detuned tone sinking into the echo bus under a faint high shimmer. Quiet by design; the kill thud already landed.

enemy_miss.what: A blow going past — one short breathy band of noise, quiet enough to read as a near thing rather than as a hit.

enemy_provoked.what: A neutral turning hostile: a short, sour two-note fall. Quiet — this fires whenever the hero makes an enemy of somebody who was not one, and it is a notification rather than a threat.

enemy_shielded.what: The blow bouncing off the shield: a hard metallic tink with no give — clearly a wall, not a wound.

enemy_shot.what: A hostile pew: lower and meaner than the hero's own shot, so return fire reads as a threat arriving, not the player's output.

enemy_slam.what: The telegraph paying off: a heavy body hitting the ground. A saw dive to the floor with a lowpass boom under it and the shockwave's dust hissing out behind — the same three-layer weight a kill gets, tuned lower and longer so it lands as a floor event rather than as a death.

enemy_summoned.what: Adds coming out of the ground: a lowpass earth-swell and a square figure climbing over it. Rises rather than falls — things are ARRIVING — and keeps a good echo send so it reads as a summoning rather than as a footstep.

enemy_telegraph.what: THE TELL — something big is about to commit. A rising detuned sawtooth wind-up under a thin bandpass hiss, so it reads as a charge building rather than as a hit landing. One sound for every telegraph kind on purpose: the player does not need to know WHICH move is coming from the audio (the telegraph is drawn), they need to know that one IS. Loud enough to cut through a fight, short enough to leave room for the move itself.

escort_arrived.what: They made it: a short relieved rising pair on a triangle, with an airy breath over the top. Deliberately modest — the objective's own completion fanfare fires on the same frame, and two fanfares are one mess.

escort_died.what: The person you were supposed to keep alive, not being alive: a low saw collapse with a hollow sine hanging after it. This is a FAILURE sting — the errand is lost — so it is allowed to be one of the bleaker sounds in the bank, and the tail is long enough to be uncomfortable.

escort_hurt.what: The person the hero is walking somewhere takes a blow: a short strained square-wave cry falling away, with a thin body-thud under it. Pitched well clear of the hero's own hurt cue so the player can tell instantly that it was not them.

footstep.what: The generic boot — the step heard on any ground nobody wrote a specific sound for. A soft, dry lowpass scuff with no character of its own, on purpose: it is the floor of the ladder, and a distinctive generic would make every unnamed surface sound like the same wrong thing. Very quiet and very short; this plays twice a second for the whole run.

footstep_dust.what: Regolith, hardpan and scrub: the powdery one. A dull lowpass puff with the cutoff well down, so it reads as a boot sinking into dust rather than landing on anything. The quietest surface in the set — most of the campaign is walked on this, so it has to disappear.

footstep_gravel.what: Loose stones underfoot: the scatter. A lowpass body with a highpass sizzle hung a few milliseconds behind it, so the step and the stones it kicked are two events rather than one — which is the whole difference between gravel and a hard floor.

footstep_metal.what: Deck plating and rusted grating: a boot on a panel that answers back. A bandpass tick of contact and a very short square ring under it — the ring is the panel flexing, and it is pitched high and cut off fast so a corridor of these does not turn into a melody.

footstep_soft.what: Carpet: the sound of a floor absorbing a boot. The dullest and quietest in the set — a very low lowpass and nothing on top of it at all. What sells it is the ABSENCE of the click every other surface has.

footstep_stone.what: Cement and bunker slab: a flat, hard slap. The lowpass body of the dust step with the cutoff opened up and a short bandpass click of grit over the top — the click is what says "hard floor" rather than "loud floor", which is why it is barely above a whisper.

footstep_void.what: Walking on nothing much: the nebula and the void deck. An airy highpass breath with a long echo send and no body under it — nothing lands, it just displaces. The one footstep in the set allowed any echo at all, because it is the one surface where the room is the point.

front_door_closed.what: The same door swinging shut: a short pull of air, the leaf meeting its frame in a low wooden thud, and the latch snapping home a moment behind it. The mirror of `front_door_opened` — everything falls where that one rises, and the latch lands LAST, which is what makes it read as shut rather than as a knock.

front_door_opened.what: A house's front door pulled open: the latch letting go with a small dry click, then a wooden hinge creaking upward as the leaf swings and the night outside comes in behind it. Quiet — a room's own door, not a bulkhead — and the rise is what says OPEN, against the fall of `front_door_closed`.

garage_door.what: The garage door rolling up: the chain drive taking up with a clack, then the long rattling climb of thirty-year-old slats on their track.

gate_entered.what: Stepping through: a swept lowpass whoosh and a sine falling away behind it. The whole sound is DEPARTURE — everything in it moves away from the listener, which is what makes it read as a transition rather than an arrival.

gate_opened.what: A way onward unlocking: a low mechanical release and a long square slide upward over it. Bigger and slower than a door — a gate is the shape of the level changing, not a room opening.

gear_repaired.what: Work done on a broken piece: two dull hammer taps on metal and a triangle note settling after them. The taps are bandpass noise rather than tone — what says "repaired" is the MATERIAL being worked, not a melody.

hay_ball_hit.what: A hay bale bumping the hero: a soft, muffled WHUMP — a low band of noise (the straw) under a short low tone (the shove), gentle so a bale caught in the lane doesn't nag on every overlap tick.

hellgate_opened.what: A HELLGATE tears open: reality ripping, not a monster arriving. A long filtered noise SWEEP up (the tear widening) under a descending tritone — the interval that refuses to resolve — capped by a sub-bass boom as whatever is on the other side steps through.

hero_down.what: A party member going down. A heavy detuned saw collapsing with a lowpass body under it, then a long hollow echo tail — the tail is what separates it from the player's own death sting: this is somebody ELSE's, heard across the room, and it should hang in the mix while the survivors decide what to do.

item_collected_ability.what: The treasure flourish — brighter and wetter for magic+ finds.

item_collected_ammo.what: Scooping up a box of ammunition — loose rounds shifting in the carton, then the pouch taking it with a short dry fourth up (G4 → C5) on a square that reads as machined rather than musical. It sits at the BOTTOM of the pickup ladder on purpose (ammo → medkit → repair → coins climb a fourth at a time, each with its own material): rounds are a stock topped up constantly, so this is the driest and lowest of the four and carries no echo at all — it has to survive being heard fifty times a level.

item_collected_drink.what: The treasure flourish — brighter and wetter for magic+ finds.

item_collected_equipment_artifact.what: The treasure flourish — brighter and wetter for magic+ finds.

item_collected_equipment_legendary.what: The treasure flourish — brighter and wetter for magic+ finds.

item_collected_equipment_magic.what: The treasure flourish — brighter and wetter for magic+ finds.

item_collected_equipment_rare.what: The treasure flourish — brighter and wetter for magic+ finds.

item_collected_equipment_regular.what: The treasure flourish — brighter and wetter for magic+ finds.

item_collected_equipment_set.what: The treasure flourish — brighter and wetter for magic+ finds.

item_collected_equipment_trash.what: The treasure flourish — brighter and wetter for magic+ finds.

item_collected_equipment_unique.what: The treasure flourish — brighter and wetter for magic+ finds.

item_collected_gold.what: Coins into the purse: the thin clink of metal on metal, then THE coin couplet — a perfect fourth leap (B5 → E6) with a glint of sine two octaves up. The top rung of the pickup ladder and the brightest of the four, but still the QUIETEST reward in the bank: a farm run walks over dozens of these a minute, so it is two notes rather than a run and its echo send stays low. Anything with a flourish on it would be unbearable by the second map.

item_collected_medkit.what: A medkit stashed into the consumable dock: soft canvas going into the pouch, then the warmest rung of the pickup ladder — a major third up (C5 → E5) on a triangle with an attack on it, so it swells rather than blips, under an octave of sine for glow. The only one of the four loose pickups with no click anywhere in it: what the hero heals with should sound like cloth and care, not like hardware. Deliberately quieter, and a THIRD where `medkitUsed` is a loud FIFTH — the satisfying mend chime belongs to the moment the kit is spent, not to finding it.

item_collected_repair.what: A repair kit stashed into the consumable dock: the toolbox latch shutting — two hard metallic clicks close together — then a bright fourth up (G5 → C6) on a detuned triangle so it rings like struck metal rather than singing. All hardware where the medkit a rung below is all cloth, which is what keeps the two dock pickups apart with your eyes shut. Kept quiet and short: the ratchet-and-ring mend belongs to `repairKitUsed`, the moment the kit is actually spent.

item_collected_xp.what: An XP SCROLL read on the run: parchment unrolling in a short dry rasp, then the script catching — a rising arcane shimmer with a bell over the top. Airier and longer than the pickups around it because it isn't a pickup, it's a spell going off, and the thirty seconds it lights are worth announcing.

item_identified.what: The scroll doing its work: a rising sine arpeggio with a glass octave over the top and a long echo — the reveal is a small ceremony, and the card that follows is the payoff. Deliberately tier-agnostic: the LOOT SHINE already says how good the piece is, and doubling that here would make identifying a blue sound like identifying an orange.

item_landed_blade.what: A blade hitting the floor: the bandpass clack of steel on stone with a bright edge ringing off it, gone in a blink. Loot lands constantly, so every voice in this family is short and sits well under a kill.

item_landed_cloth.what: Cloth landing: a soft flump and nothing else. The quietest drop in the game — a robe hitting regolith barely makes a sound, and that contrast is what makes mail and plate read as heavy.

item_landed_coin.what: A purse coming apart on the floor: a bright metallic chime with a second, lower one a beat behind it, over a short hiss of loose change settling. Not one object landing — several, which is what tells it apart from the trinket's single tink.

item_landed_flask.what: Glass on stone: two close sine partials beating against each other for the clink, with a bright chip of contact under them. Medkits and drinks both land on it.

item_landed_gun.what: A gun going down: the dull thunk of a heavy receiver, a metallic clack of the action, and the tiniest spring ping behind it.

item_landed_leather.what: Leather hitting the ground: a slap with a creak in its tail. Duller and a touch longer than cloth, with a low body cloth doesn't have.

item_landed_mail.what: Mail landing: not one impact but a hundred small ones — three bright chips of link-on-link a beat apart over a thin ring. The jingle is the whole read; a single clack would just be plate again.

item_landed_plate.what: Plate armor going down — the heaviest landing in the game: a low clang with a real body under it, a broad metal wash, and enough echo that it reads as something big rather than something loud.

item_landed_relic.what: A story piece coming to rest: a low resonant hum that swells rather than strikes, wet with echo. Rare enough to be allowed the length.

item_landed_scrap.what: A repair kit's toolbox clatter: two bandpass chips a beat apart over a blunt square thunk. Junk, and it should sound like junk.

item_landed_spark.what: A charged pickup settling — an XP scroll or a powerup canister: a quick rising ting with a hiss of static, so the energy reads before the weight does.

item_landed_trinket.what: A ring, an amulet or a charm going down: one tiny metallic tink with a breath of sizzle. Small object, small sound.

item_landed_wand.what: A wand or a staff knocking down: a hollow wooden tap with a thin crystal shimmer sitting on top of it.

jump.what: The rising boing (moon gravity edition), with a soft sine top.

knockout_recovered.what: He shakes it off and gets up: a quick, light rising triangle — relief, not fanfare, well under the hurt ceiling.

lair_opened.what: Something's home opening up: a deep lowpass groan with a slow detuned saw under it and a heavy echo send. Low, long, and unfriendly — this is an invitation the player should feel slightly bad about accepting.

land.what: Boots in regolith: a dull lowpass puff.

level_up.what: The DING — the game's biggest triumph, sized to fill the engine's ding-celebration window (LEVELING.dingCelebrationMs) while the light EXPLODES off the hero and the horde is hurled back, so sound and light are one moment. Anatomy of the triumph, ground-up: 1. THE DETONATION — a deep sub-boom the instant the light bursts: a low sine dropping into the floor under a soft filtered thump, so the ding lands with WEIGHT before the fanfare lifts off it.

lightning.what: The storm strike: a bright crack, a falling zap, thunder in the echo.

loot_shine_artifact.what: The red-white find, and the rarest sound in the game: a sub swell, a full rising figure over it, and a long shimmering tail. It is allowed to be the biggest thing on screen because a player may go a whole campaign without hearing it.

loot_shine_legendary.what: The orange find: the unique's arpeggio taken a step further and given a floor — a low saw swell rises underneath the bells so the moment has weight as well as sparkle.

loot_shine_magic.what: The blue find: one soft sine bell over the thud, and no more than that. Magic items are common enough that the flourish has to stay a hint.

loot_shine_rare.what: The yellow find: two bells stepping up. The first interval in the family — a rare says "and there is more" where a magic just says "look".

loot_shine_set.what: The green find: a three-note triangle figure, warmer and rounder than the rare's sines — a set piece is a collection, so it arrives as a phrase rather than as a step.

loot_shine_unique.what: The gold find — the one every Diablo player learns to hear from across a room: a bright four-note major arpeggio with a shimmer over the top, and enough echo to hang for a beat after the item has settled.

medkit_used.what: Spending a kit: the warm two-note mend (a major fifth up) with a soft octave glow — the satisfying "patched up" chime. A bigger kit (`tier` ≥ LARGE) rings a brighter bell on top so the grade is audible.

menace_rose.what: The horde evolves: a dark, rising swell — three detuned sawtooth steps climbing a minor triad under a low growl, so a rampage feels answered rather than rewarded.

merchant_discovered.what: Finding somebody selling something out here: a bright little three-note triangle flourish with a coin-bright sine on the end. It is one of the few genuinely GOOD surprises a level hands out, so it is allowed to be a small fanfare — but a short one, and well under a boss's.

merchant_run_down.what: A body goes under the car. The heaviest, wettest impact in the game and the only one with no weapon in it: a bandpass thump of the bumper arriving, a lowpass boom of the mass going down under the wheels, and a short scrape of tyre over tarmac coming out the far side of it. Rare enough to be big — it happens at most once a visit — but no shot at the top of the mix: the drive-out's engine is running under it and this has to land INSIDE that rather than over it.

mercy_drop.what: The guardian's arrival: a soft, consonant halo of sound — a rising major arpeggio of sine bells (C6–E6–G6–C7) under a shimmering high sine, all wet with echo. Gentle (a rescue, not a fanfare) and pitched above the drop's own tick so the two layer rather than clash.

meteor_fall.what: MOONFALL landing: a dead-weight rock hitting regolith — a low lowpassed thud with a short gravel crack over it. No ring: this is stone, not ordnance, and it repeats every half second, so it stays dry.

nova.what: A NOVA proc: a short arcane whump — a low burst and a rising shimmer, deliberately smaller than the nuke (procs fire often).

nuke.what: The screen-clearer: sub detonation, long lowpass rumble, and a falling scream, all sent to the echo so it hangs in the air.

pack_awoken.what: The ambush sting: a pack boils up out of the ground. A short, low menace growl — a saw dropping under a detuned square stab, dusted with a gritty noise burst — threatening, but a notch under a boss arrival.

pack_cleared.what: The all-clear: this patch of ground is yours. A bright, brief rising two-note affirmation with a glass octave — satisfying without reaching for the boss-kill or level-clear fanfare.

parry.what: A blow turned aside on steel: a bright metallic clang — a high bandpassed tick over a quick ringing tone that snaps shut.

pickup_blocked.what: You may not have that: a short, flat, slightly sour square blip that does not resolve. The refusal has to be instantly distinguishable from the pickup it is refusing, so it is the same register and the OPPOSITE gesture — the pickups all rise, and this one sits still.

player_death.what: THE FALL — the fatal blow lands and the hero drops. A hard, dull body thud into the dust (a filtered low-noise punch under a short sub-drop), then a slow, sinking doom tone opening the death scene. The mournful `defeat` fanfare comes later, with the modal.

player_dodge.what: A clean sidestep: a short airy whiff sweeping up and out of the way, no impact body — the blow that never landed.

player_hurt.what: Must cut through everything: a wide detuned saw buzz dropping to the sub register, with a dull body-impact under it. Mix ceiling.

player_phased.what: A blow passing clean through the spectral hero: a breath of air where a hit should have been. Deliberately almost nothing — the ABSENCE of the usual thud is the feedback.

pod_opened.what: A pod cracking: a pressurised hiss venting, then the shell letting go with a bandpass clack. The hiss leads because that is the part that says SEALED — the clack alone would just be a crate.

projectile_bounced.what: A shot coming off a wall instead of stopping: a thin, bright bandpass tick with a short square ring. Very quiet — a ricochet is information about geometry, and in a firefight it happens constantly.

quest_accepted.what: The errand is taken on: a short paper-and-ink figure — a dry parchment rustle under two clipped square notes a fourth apart, rising. Deliberately small and dry, because ACCEPTING is the start of the work; the fanfare belongs to finishing it.

quest_completed.what: Every objective is met — the WoW "quest complete" beat, and the one moment the system gets a real fanfare: a four-note rising figure (C, E, G, high C) in triangle, each note shadowed an octave up by a quiet sine, with a bright hiss over the top and a shimmer rising out of the tail. Louder and longer than the accept cue on purpose: this is the sound the player is working for.

quest_failed.what: The errand is lost — today only an escort who fell. A falling minor third in a dull square wave with a low thud under it: no sting, no alarm. The player already watched somebody die; the cue only has to confirm it counted.

quest_giver_met.what: Somebody with an errand notices the hero: a soft two-note greeting on a sine, quieter than the merchant's till — this is a person looking up, not a shop opening.

quest_piece_bought.what: Coins leaving the purse for something the errand needed: a short coin chitter and a triangle note under it, falling. Money going OUT falls; money coming in rises (see quest_piece_sold).

quest_piece_sold.what: Coins arriving: the same chitter and the same triangle, rising instead. The pair is deliberately one sound played two ways — a player should be able to tell a purchase from a sale with their eyes shut, and direction is the cheapest possible way to say it.

quest_progress.what: A tally moved: one clipped high tick, a tally mark going down on paper. Under a twentieth of the completion cue's volume — this fires once per kill on a long errand, so it has to sit UNDER the combat rather than on top of it.

quest_restocked.what: The stall filling up again: a soft double triangle tap, low and unhurried. Bookkeeping the player may want to notice and must never be bothered by, so it sits near the bottom of the mix.

quest_turned_in.what: The handover and the payout: a warm coin-and-thanks figure — a low triangle settling under two bright chimes, with a little purse rattle of filtered noise. Warmer and shorter than the completion fanfare, because the celebration already happened; this is the reward landing in the hand.

repair_kit_used.what: Spending a repair kit: the toolbox at work — two ratchet clicks, then the mended edge rings bright (the chime that used to fire on pickup).

scorch_burn.what: Standing in something that is still burning: a short highpass sizzle with a faint low ember under it. This repeats while the hero is in the fire, so it is among the quietest and shortest sounds in the bank — a texture, not an alarm. The damage numbers are the alarm.

seismic_landing.what: A warlord's touchdown slams the ground: a heavy low boom under a gravelly lowpass crunch — the shockwave the SEISMIC LANDING talent rings.

shot_magic.what: An arcane zap: detuned triangle rise with a shimmer tail.

shot_ranged.what: An arcane zap: detuned triangle rise with a shimmer tail.

shot_sawed_off.what: Both barrels at once: a sub-heavy boom under a lowpass powder blast, a sharp crack of the report on top, and the shot sizzling away after it. The class `shot_ranged` zap is a pea-shooter beside it — the opening weapon of the gentlest rung is meant to land like a door being kicked in, so it sits above every other weapon in the mix and stays under `player_hurt`, which is the ceiling. Named by the weapon itself (`WeaponDef.sfx`), not by an event shape.

singularity.what: An ARCANE SINGULARITY collapse: the inverse of a nova — a DOWNward in-rush whoosh that swallows itself, tuned pitch falling as the vortex draws the swarm into its core.

spare_offered.what: A beaten unique kneels and the verdict lands on the table: a held low question mark — two slow detuned steps that don't resolve, hanging in the echo until the player answers.

spawner_alarmed.what: A nest noticing the hero: a two-pulse alarm, square and mechanical, on a falling interval. It is a warning the player can act on — the nest is about to start producing — so it is dry and legible rather than atmospheric.

stamina_potion_used.what: Draining a stamina potion: a fizzy hiss cracking open, then a quick two-note lift as the legs come back under the hero.

story_item_collected.what: A plot piece: a slow, reverent rise left hanging in the echo.

swing.what: Air being cut: a band-shaped whoosh over a low triangle thunk.

talk_opened.what: Somebody has something to say: a soft two-note triangle rise, quieter and rounder than a menu confirm. It opens a conversation rather than a window, so it is warm rather than clicky.

ui_back.what: The confirm inverted: two falling steps, drier.

ui_blip.what: The letter-print tick: the dry, quiet square pip heard under scrolling 16-bit dialogue as each character lands. Fired many times per line, so it stays the shortest and softest voice in the set — a whisper of a chip pulse, never a menu blip's full "blip".

ui_boom.what: The title sun going supernova: the star COLLAPSES first — a short, rising, sucking sweep — and everything else lands 150ms later on the white-out flash: a cracking sub-detonation, a long lowpass rumble that rolls out under it, and a falling scream, all pushed into the echo bus so the blast hangs in the air. The title screen's loudest moment by design — a secret payoff, not a menu tick.

ui_confirm.what: Two rising detuned steps: "accepted", with a little room on it.

ui_equip.what: Two blades crossing: a metallic double-clang. Each strike is a bright bandpass noise chink under a pair of inharmonic steel partials (the non-octave 3:2-ish ratio is what reads as "metal", not "note"); the parry lands a beat after the first strike and rings out into the echo bus for the WoW-style "shiiing".

ui_guide.what: The "go this way" beacon: a soft sonar ping in step with the guidance arrow's blink (~once a second while the way is clear). A gentle sine pulse with a glassy octave sparkle and a breath of echo — it sits at the very bottom of the mix, a nudge onward, never an alert. Repeats often, so it stays among the quietest and shortest voices in the set.

ui_move.what: A dry cursor blip with a glassy octave on top.

ui_shutter.what: A camera shutter: the leaf snapping open and, a breath later, closed — two bright, dry noise clicks with a tiny mechanical tick between them. Short and quiet enough to fire mid-fight without stepping on the weapon it interrupts.

ui_start.what: The run-start fanfare: a brassy rising arpeggio over a root, capped with a snare — a two-second console "here we go".

victory.what: The triumph fanfare: brass squares over a held triangle root, capped with a snare — the full parade.

void_wave.what: THE UNMAKING: a swell that falls away instead of rising — a descending sine under a wide, filtered wash, so the wave reads as taking something out of the room rather than adding to it.

ward_held.what: CONTINUITY PROTOCOL refusing a killing blow — the single most important beat a run has. A struck gold bell over a rising swell, wet with echo: the one powerup sound written to be unmistakable through everything else happening at the moment the hero should have died.

weapon_broke.what: Something giving out: a metallic crack, a ping of shrapnel, and the pieces sagging away down a saw drop. Armor wearing through shares the weapon's snap — same "your kit just failed" alarm, same urgency.

weapon_dry.what: The empty gun: a dry mechanical CLICK and nothing behind it. The single most important piece of feedback the game was missing — a trigger pull that does nothing has to be audibly different from one that missed, or the player reads "out of ammo" as "the game dropped my input". Deliberately thin and toneless: it is the sound of a mechanism moving with no charge to answer it.

well_death.what: The hole swallows the HERO: the swallow dive, longer and lower, with a heavier low rumble behind it — the same spiral, but this one is fatal.

well_swallowed.what: A black hole swallows a mob: a deep spiral down into nothing — a sine dive with a swallowed puff of filtered noise.
